first_understanding_order.objective: Establish exact singleton/global-return contracts before reading callers.
first_understanding_order.why_first: Named plus decomp-backed; highest-certainty contract roots with many evidenced dependents.

first_understanding_order.objective: Characterize the unnamed high-fan-in contracts; do not yet assign singleton meanings without body/global evidence.
first_understanding_order.why_first: They are the largest gameplay dependency bottlenecks and are not decomp-backed.

first_understanding_order.objective: Map manager getters, setters, and update/continuation functions before subsystem bodies.
first_understanding_order.why_first: Managers are explicit name-bearing lifecycle/state hubs.

first_understanding_order.objective: Freeze cross-category contracts used by the most bridge-heavy functions.
first_understanding_order.why_first: Bridge call edges expose where semantic gameplay work enters engine/runtime implementation.

first_understanding_order.objective: Separate dispatch/control flow from leaf algorithms by reading top orchestrators and vtable-backed handlers.
first_understanding_order.why_first: High fan-out/vtable functions encode sequencing and boundary decisions.

first_understanding_order.objective: Study clusters only after root, manager, and bridge contracts; prioritize coherent clusters with decomp coverage and gameplay content.
first_understanding_order.why_first: Cluster totals are direct membership counts; no runtime order is asserted.

first_understanding_order.objective: Parallelize call-isolated functions, prioritizing gameplay, named, decomp-backed rows.
first_understanding_order.why_first: They have no canonical call dependency to another function or external import, so they do not block the graph roots.

gameplay_engine_bridges.edge_list_scope: Ranked evidence slices only. Complete edge set remains the canonical TSV; aggregate counts above cover all rows.

method.bridge_definition: Internal call pair whose caller/callee categories span gameplay and engine/runtime boundaries as named in bridge_counts.
method.chokepoint_definition: sqrt(distinct internal callers * distinct internal callees), requiring >=5 callers and >=1 callee. Proxy only; not exact betweenness.
method.components_definition: Weak components and SCCs use only direct-call/thunk/computed-call edges whose callee is a pinned triage function. External, vtable-ref, and data-ref rows do not join function components.
method.degree_definition: Distinct internal caller/callee pairs; external targets counted separately; multiple callsites never inflate degree.
method.edge_policy: Every emitted function-to-function edge contains canonical types and actual callsites. Vtable refs to VT: bases and data refs are not promoted to calls or runtime ordering.
method.isolated_definition: No distinct internal caller, no internal callee, and no external call target. Reference-only isolates are separately counted because vtable/data references are retained but not call dependencies.
method.orchestrator_definition: Rank by distinct internal plus external callees; category and vtable evidence disambiguate dispatch.
method.ranking_tie_break: Metric descending, then VA ascending; bridge functions use total bridge degree descending, fan-in descending, VA ascending.
method.root_definition: Named singleton candidates require singleton_regex + gameplay category + callers. Unnamed root candidates require gameplay + >=8 callers + <=4 internal callees. These are ranked candidates, not asserted state semantics.
method.semantic_component_definition: The exhaustive 20-cluster taxonomy in tools/triage/classify.py::_row_cluster, recomputed from triage-v6 rows; descriptions are structural, not runtime sequence.
method.wrapper_forest_definition: Target fan forests count callers with <=4 total internal callees and <=2 remaining after target removal. Vtable-backed high-fan-out functions form a separate dispatch forest.

title: Track I global call-graph and dependency archaeology

unresolved_graph_limitations.impact: A vtable-ref row points to the containing vtable base, not the exact selected slot method. No caller-to-slot virtual-call edge is invented.
The binary has no MSVC RTTI; the candidate inventory has 3,081 candidates but only 20 labels. Vtable families can merge or misattribute.
The exporter retains data refs only when the target is itself a pinned function or a known vtable range. Shared-state candidates cannot be proven from reads/writes to globals in this artifact.
A call xref proves a reference, not that a route is runtime-reachable on every execution. Tail calls, thunks, and computed-call semantics are not fully resolved here.
unresolved_graph_limitations.limitation: call reference is not execution proof

unresolved_graph_limitations.impact: External edges identify imported functions, not the third-party implementation or its complete dependency graph.
39,716 functions remain UNKNOWN; v6 region/caller propagation is static inference. Bridges and semantic components inherit those category assignments.
Only 1,667 functions have exported SDK decompilation; most high-fan-in unnamed roots have no body artifact. Root semantics beyond names/contracts remain unresolved.
The triage projection has zero OBSERVED and zero VERIFIED functions. First-understanding order is structural, not a runtime call sequence.
